citacoes.p0: Recognized by the Higher Education Chamber of the National Council of Education, with qualification in Art History, Visual Arts and Art Education, granted by the Federal Council of Education — MEC, 1995/1996.
citacoes.p1: “I cannot combine certain characters dhcmrlchtdj that the divine Library has not foreseen and that in none of its secret languages do not contain a terrible meaning. No one can articulate a syllable that is not full of tenderness and fears; that is not, in one of those languages, the powerful name of a god. To speak is to incur tautologies.”
citacoes.p2: “A 'highly cohesive' body of work that, constituted over three decades, has always been marked by its experimental, irreverent and reflexive character, by its transit through diverse media and artistic languages, by the crossing of different domains, bodies of knowledge and sensibilities.”
citacoes.p3: “We see through enigmas, we hear through dissonances. It is this place outside place that Barja never ceases to open. That is why I suspect that this writing-art alongside is, above all, ‘artesemnome.’”
citacoes.p4: “The artist becomes a creator when an explorer of concepts, materialized through construction, the subtle and irreplaceable balance of visuality, at the limit of image and word.”
citacoes.p5: “Barja remains faithful to the listening of that place, of that space where the past converts itself into a new thought, a new form; not through sublimation, but through the illumination of a place and of the word that is kept within it, where the culture of European origin, Brazilian nature and African sap fuse.”
citacoes.p6: “An ironic and lucid association between the crossings of São João and Beuys: both prophets in the desert, announcing a message whose complete meaning has sense only in the future, by virtue of subsequent events.”
